subject: Immediate: Quantized model rollout causing 429/5xx surge
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Incident] sudden 429/5xx spike after quantized v2 rollout

Folks,

Quick heads-up — Canary cluster C-7 shows a dramatic jump in 429 and 5xx responses starting ~08:45 PT after the scheduled rollout of the quantized v2 artifact (qv2-kernelB). Error mix is predominantly 429 (client throttles/timeouts) + a smaller but growing set of 500s from the runtime kernel path. The perf dashboard is attached and I pulled top logs into top-logs-429s.txt.

What I can see so far:
- 08:40 — rollouts started (10% traffic to qv2).
- 08:45 — latency median up 2.3x; 429 rate jumps from 0.4% -> 6.8%.
- 08:52 — Some workers throw kernel mismatch tracebacks and restart loops.

Immediate asks:
1) Rishi / Markus: can we pause the rollout and fail traffic back to prior model variant?
2) Evelyn / Ops: can you correlate autoscaler activity — are we seeing retry storms from SDK clients?
3) Laura: FYI for account outreach. I’ll notify Veridian if this persists.

Attachments: perf-dashboard.png, top-logs-429s.txt, canary-config-diff.patch

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
SRE, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] sudden 429/5xx spike after quantized v2 rollout

On Tue, Jun 2, 2026 at 09:12 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick heads-up — Canary cluster C-7 shows a dramatic jump in 429 and 5xx responses starting ~08:45 PT after the scheduled rollout of the quantized v2 artifact (qv2-kernelB).

I'll pause the canary rollout now and route 100% back to qv1. Pausing via rollout controller (will push rollback in ~2m).

Preliminary hypothesis: the quantization profile for qv2 reduced memory margin under the new kernel B path, which combined with our exponential-retry SDK heuristics produced local queueing and then client-side throttling (429). Also seeing a hot shard on GPU-2 in C-7.

Actions I’m taking:
- Pausing rollout and replacing qv2 instances with qv1 equivalents (in flight).
- Draining C-7 tasks off kernel B nodes.
- Collecting kernel-level traces and perf counters.

If rollback doesn't reduce 429 within 5m we should open a P1 with SRE and loop in infra for kernel artifact re-evaluation.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Incident] sudden 429/5xx spike after quantized v2 rollout

Thanks — Rishi, prioritize immediate rollback. Laura, please draft a short proactive note to Veridian engineering and their CRO (Maya). Keep it factual and state we are rolling back and investigating; ask them not to escalate to executive ops yet — we will update within 1 hour.

Evelyn: ask CS to open an incident bridge and invite Veridian's platform-eng. Include the runbook link and the recent canary diffs (attached).

I’m standing by if you need approvals for credits or SLA exceptions.

— Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success & Operations
From: Maya Patel <maya@veridian.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-eng@veridian.ai
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:45:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Serving issue impacting inference at Veridian (429 surge)

Thanks for the heads-up. We are seeing elevated client retry rates on our side too and some customer-facing latency spikes. Please keep us updated on the rollback status and any required config changes.

A few asks from us:
- Can you confirm whether the change was only quantization + kernel flag, or were there other micro-opt changes?
- If this is expected to affect other customers, please flag scope.

We’re on standby on the bridge.

— Maya Patel
CRO, Veridian AI
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: platform-eng@veridian.ai, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:01:30 -07:00
Subject: Incident bridge + initial findings (JIRA-ISSUE-1298)

Bridge: zoom.us/j/999-888-777 (incident bridge)

Summary of initial findings:
- Rollback deployed at 09:25 PT and fully active across canaries by 09:28 PT.
- 429 rate returned to baseline (~0.6%) by 09:37 PT on C-7.
- Kernel B nodes exhibited elevated page-fault stalls when quantized layers hit certain sequence-lengths; kernel stack traces attached in top-logs-429s.txt.
- Evidence of client retry amplification: several clients with default SDK retry config produced dense bursts at 08:47–08:53, amplifying transient latency into 429s.

Next steps:
1) Rishi + Runtime: capture a reproducible perf test (seq-len distribution match) and run qv2 with kernel B under controlled load.
2) Engineering: add a temporary circuit-breaker to the rollout controller to detect 5%+ 429 within 5 minutes and auto-pause.
3) Product/CS: coordinate a concise customer note and optional credit offering if SLA hit.

Attaching: perf-dashboard.png, top-logs-429s.txt, canary-config-diff.patch

— Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Reliability
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@veridian.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Rivers <paul@acadiaops.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: qv2 kernel regression postmortem & mitigation plan

Maya / Veridian team —

Thanks again for patience while we investigated. Short summary and action items:

What happened:
- We rolled out qv2 (quantization profile + kernel B) to a canary at 08:40 PT on 2026-06-02.
- A combination of reduced memory headroom under kernel B for certain sequence-length distributions, plus client-side retry amplification, caused transient queuing and a spike in 429/5xx responses.

Impact:
- Veridian: 30 minutes of elevated client retries/latency; no data leak or incorrect model outputs reported.

Immediate mitigations completed:
- Rollback executed at 09:25 PT; metrics returned to baseline by 09:37 PT.
- Temporary rollback block implemented in deployment pipeline for qv2 variants until artifacts pass extended perf gating.

Planned fixes / next steps:
1) Rishi: run extended perf matrix for qv2+kernel B (seq-len sweeps, batch profiles) and publish results to JIRA-ISSUE-1298 by EOD 2026-06-04.
2) Stephanie/Evelyn: run a canary with adjusted SDK retry window and a stricter circuit-breaker in the rollout controller.
3) Laura/CS: send a customer update and offer a one-time SLA credit if Veridian records >5% SLO breach during the incident window.
4) Ops/Infra: add kernel-level telemetry to the rollout gating pipeline so page-fault stalls or unusual perf counters fail canary promotion.

We will follow up with a draft postmortem (link above) and a proposed timeline for reintroducing qv2 safely.

Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success & Operations
Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: perf-dashboard.png, top-logs-429s.txt, canary-config-diff.patch
